_doc: Independent reference oracle, money kind. Asserts that PetTaperCharge charges a failed potentially exempt transfer as gov.uk and IHTA 1984 say: tax on the part of the gift above the nil-rate band still available after earlier chargeable transfers (cumulation, s.7(1)), at 40% reduced by taper relief for the band of years between gift and death (s.7(4)), and nothing for a gift made seven years or more before the death (s.3A(4)). One gift per case: available_nil_rate_band is the band left after the transfers made before it, which is how the gov.uk Sally example works through her three gifts. The gift-to-death interval is an input in the statute's own bands; turning two dates into a band is the caller's job. Not asserted, deliberately: chargeable lifetime transfers and the s.7(5) floor, which gov.uk does not work an example of. Figures read from gov.uk and legislation.gov.uk on sourced_at.
statute: IHTA 1984 s.3A(4) (PET exempt after seven years), s.7(1) (cumulation), s.7(4) (taper relief)

cases.label: sally-brother-9-years
cases.citation_quote: There's no Inheritance Tax to pay on the £50,000 gift to her brother as it was given more than 7 years before she died.
cases.note: IHTA 1984 s.3A(4): a PET made seven years or more before the death is exempt, so it is not a chargeable transfer and does not use the nil-rate band of the later gifts.

cases.label: sally-sister-4y2m-within-threshold
cases.citation_quote: There's also no Inheritance Tax to pay on the £325,000 she gave her sister, as this is within the Inheritance Tax threshold.
cases.note: Given 4 years and 2 months before death (s.7(4)(b) band), but £325,000 does not exceed the £325,000 available, so there is no tax to taper. This gift leaves no nil-rate band for the next one (cumulation, s.7(1)).

cases.label: sally-friend-3-to-4-years-nrb-used
cases.citation_quote: But her friend must pay Inheritance Tax on her £100,000 gift at a rate of 32%, as it's above the tax-free threshold and was given 3 years before Sally died. The Inheritance Tax due is £32,000.
cases.note: Cumulation: the sister's earlier £325,000 used the whole nil-rate band, so available_nil_rate_band is £0. gov.uk applies the 32% (3 to 4 years) rate, which under s.7(4)(a) means the gift was made more than three years before the death; the band input says so. £100,000 × 40% × 80% = £32,000.

cases.label: band-NotMoreThanThreeYears-100k-above-threshold
cases.citation_quote: Gifts given in the 3 years before your death are taxed at 40%. Gifts given 3 to 7 years before your death are taxed on a sliding scale known as 'taper relief'.
cases.note: £100,000 above the threshold taxed at the gov.uk rate 40% = £40,000. Statute: IHTA 1984 s.7(4) (full rate within three years) of the 40% rate.

cases.label: band-MoreThanThreeNotMoreThanFourYears-100k-above-threshold
cases.note: £100,000 above the threshold taxed at the gov.uk rate 32% = £32,000. Statute: IHTA 1984 s.7(4)(a), 80 per cent of the 40% rate.

cases.label: band-MoreThanFourNotMoreThanFiveYears-100k-above-threshold
cases.note: £100,000 above the threshold taxed at the gov.uk rate 24% = £24,000. Statute: IHTA 1984 s.7(4)(b), 60 per cent of the 40% rate.

cases.label: band-MoreThanFiveNotMoreThanSixYears-100k-above-threshold
cases.note: £100,000 above the threshold taxed at the gov.uk rate 16% = £16,000. Statute: IHTA 1984 s.7(4)(c), 40 per cent of the 40% rate.

cases.label: band-MoreThanSixLessThanSevenYears-100k-above-threshold
cases.note: £100,000 above the threshold taxed at the gov.uk rate 8% = £8,000. Statute: IHTA 1984 s.7(4)(d), 20 per cent of the 40% rate.
